label: <DEL> step of length-9 sequences starting with p or 1
explanation: A very sparse feature (43 of 500k dev sequences). It fires only at the delimiter step, which is also the step where original token 0 is output, and almost only when L = 9 (42 of 43; one weak activation at L = 8). It also needs the first original token, i.e. the token about to be output, to be p (75% of activation mass) or 1 (24%). Its few other activations are weak and start with o or 2. It never fires in the original or copy phases. The predicate covers 99% of activation mass, but precision is under 1%: the feature fires on only a small fraction of the qualifying sequences. Active sequences often contain the letter e two or more times, and the strongest ones mostly start with p and contain e. Requiring two or more e tokens raises precision to about 17% but loses about half the mass, so what selects the subset is unresolved and probably depends on the distributed hidden state. Magnitude is highest for p-initial sequences that contain e; top activation 1.14 on p 1 r e n o e l s.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 18 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=p (+3.51), phase=1 & out_tok=1 (+3.13), orig4=e (+2.33), orig3=e (+1.90), next_out=1 (+1.57), orig2=f (+1.51). Lower it: orig8=- (-2.54), in_count=1 (-2.24), in_first=0 (-1.82), n_digits=1 (-0.67).
